lines.text: This frog freezes solid. Then it comes back to life.
And that's not even the weird part.
Every winter, the wood frog lets up to sixty percent of its body turn into ice.
lines.caption: Every winter, the wood frog lets up to 60% of its body turn into ice.

lines.text: Its heart stops beating. It stops breathing.
Its secret? It floods its body with sugar, a natural antifreeze that protects its cells.
And the weird part? In tests, Alaskan wood frogs survived minus eighteen degrees, frozen for up to two hundred and eighteen days. Then in spring, they thaw and hop away.
lines.caption: And the weird part? In tests, Alaskan wood frogs survived −18 °C, frozen for up to 218 days. Then in spring, they thaw and hop away.
